references.text: God commands Noah to enter the ark with his family to avoid judgment, paralleling how Lot is urged to take his family out of Sodom.
Abraham's intercession for the righteous in Sodom sets the background for the angels rescuing Lot and his family from destruction.
Lot goes to his sons-in-law (chatan, see v.12) and warns them, but they think he is joking.
The angels hurry Lot and his family out of the city to avoid being struck by the judgment on Sodom.
Jesus uses Lot's time and the destruction of Sodom as an example of sudden judgment, relevant to the angels' warning to leave the city.
Peter refers to Lot as a righteous man who was rescued from the destruction of Sodom, describing God's ability to deliver the godly from trials.
The letter of Jude mentions Sodom and Gomorrah as examples of God's judgment with eternal fire, paralleling the rescue of Lot.
Proverbs 11:8 illustrates the theological principle unfolding in the case of Lot: the righteous are saved, the wicked are punished.
Isaiah 30:18 highlights God's patient grace in the case of Lot: God delays judgment to make room for salvation.
Psalm 37:40 confirms the theological principle in the case of Lot: The Lord rescues those who take refuge in Him.
Psalm 7:10 illustrates the theological principle in the case of Lot: God's judgment on the wickedness of the evil saves the righteous.
Psalm 7:9 highlights the theological principle in the case of Lot: God's ability to distinguish between the righteous and the wicked in judgment.
Psalm 98:9 shows that God's judgment on Sodom in the case of Lot is a precursor to His global judgment over the earth.
Psalm 71:2 confirms the theological principle in the case of Lot: God's righteousness is the foundation of salvation.
Proverbs 13:21 illustrates the theological principle unfolding in the case of Lot: the righteous are rewarded, the wicked punished.
Psalm 51:3 highlights God's grace and mercy in the Lot incident: God sends angels to rescue Lot.
Psalm 76:10 affirms the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's salvation is available to the humble.
Psalm 96:13 shows that God's judgment on Sodom in the Lot incident is a precursor to His global judgment over the earth.
Ezekiel 37:23 illuminates the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's ability to save from sin and injustice.
Psalm 82:4 confirms the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's care for the weak and needy.
Daniel 6:28 affirms the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's ability to save from death.
Psalm 64:11 confirms the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's salvation is available to the righteous.
Isaiah 1:10 shows that God's judgment on Sodom in the Lot incident is a warning to other cities.
Micah 7:9 affirms the theological principle in the Lot incident: God's justice is available to those who seek refuge in Him.
Ezekiel 16:49 explains the cause of God's judgment on Sodom in the Lot incident: Sodom's sin.
Revelation 19:2 shows that God's judgment on Sodom in the Lot incident is a precursor to His global judgment.
